title: Artificial intelligence
audience: a college student in a computer science degree program, or a career changer studying the same material on their own
purpose: Learn the main ideas of artificial intelligence: agents and problem formulation, uninformed and heuristic search, local search, adversarial search, constraint satisfaction, logic and knowledge representation, planning, Bayesian networks, Markov decision processes, reinforcement learning, and an introduction to machine learning, large language models and AI ethics.
primary_reading: Artificial Intelligence: Foundations of Computational Agents by Poole and Mackworth (free online)

weeks.2: Uninformed search: BFS, DFS and uniform-cost search
weeks.3: Heuristic search: A* and admissible heuristics
weeks.5: Adversarial search: minimax and alpha–beta pruning
weeks.12: Machine learning, large language models and AI ethics

blocks.deliverable: Formulate and solve a puzzle with search.
Week 7 midterm; solve a CSP with backtracking and forward checking.
Compute state values with value iteration.
Implement Q-learning on a small grid world.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Game-playing or planning agent: implement an agent for a supplied environment (for example Connect Four or a grid world) using search or reinforcement learning, evaluate it against simple baselines, and write a report that includes the limitations and risks of the approach.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
